news.title: UEFA threatens World Cup boycott, putting Infantino under pressure
news.lede: The president of FIFA, Gianni Infantino, who had previously presented Donald Trump with a "Peace Prize" in a lavish ceremony, has just triggered an all-out war on the international football stage. On Thursday, July 30, two days after the international football governing body and its ever-present president announced a project – devised in utmost secrecy by the elite of the global football world – to create a commercial company bringing together its main economic assets, including the rights to the World Cup, to open its capital to private investors and increase its profits, the European football governing body (UEFA) pushed back. At the end of an emergency meeting of its 55 national member federations, held online to discuss the controversial project which is seen as auctioning off shares of the World Cup to private investors, UEFA fired back with the threat of a boycott.

news.title: Gianni Infantino's top aide's damning statement in full after QUITTING over 'irresponsible' World Cup sale plot
news.lede: A SENIOR adviser to Fifa chief Gianni Infantino has released a damning statement after resigning in protest over their World Cup sell-off plan. Former US Soccer president and Goldman Sachs vice-chair Carlos Cordeiro suddenly stepped down from his role as an aide to the controversial executive on Friday. The move came in response to Fifa’s proposal to create a subsidiary company called the Fifa Forward Enterprise, which would oversee the World Cup. Private investors would then be able to purchase stakes in the company, essentially taking ownership of a chunk of the World Cup.

news.title: Uefa has formed a rare but fragile united front against Fifa in battle for football’s future | Nick Ames and Matt Hughes
news.lede: Emerging from this week with unity over Fifa’s World Cup sell off was quite an acheivement but Europe cannot rest on its laurels. It was a phrase not always heard when Europe’s football associations discuss a pressing issue. “Touchingly unanimous,” was the assessment of a senior Uefa executive within moments of Thursday afternoon’s seismic decision to boycott Fifa tournaments unless Gianni Infantino scraps his private investment plan. United fronts on this scale are vanishingly rare and there is now a narrow window in which to make it count.

news.title: UEFA to boycott World Cup if Infantino sell-off plan goes ahead
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. England, its fellow UEFA nations and CONCACAF have unanimously voted to boycott the upcoming men’s and women’s World Cups if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with plans to sell off shares in the tournament to private investors. UEFA’s 55 member nations held a virtual crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss Infantino’s recently announced plans to privatise and sell shares in the World Cup.
